author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

title: Woman Walks Free From Pig Farrowing Crate After 21 Days And Nights In Trafalgar Square
content:
Animal Rising vows further factory farm exposés as group says three-week action marks beginning of long-term campaign to end factory farming.

Animal Rising campaign lead Michelle Farnham has today (22 September) walked free from a pig farrowing crate in Trafalgar Square after spending 21 consecutive days and nights confined inside it, without leaving once.

Michelle emerged from the crate at 11am, after first entering it at 7am on 1 September, completing an extraordinary physical and psychological challenge designed to bring the reality of factory farming into public view.

She greeted a crowd of approximately 100 supporters and was joined by her partner and family following the three weeks of intense isolation.

Thousands of passersby encountered the installation during its three weeks in one of London’s busiest public spaces, with many stopping to speak with Michelle about the action and the conditions faced by animals in factory farms.

The action attracted national and international media attention, with high-profile visitors including former RSPCA president Chris Packham and Green MP Adrian Ramsay. [1]

title: Animal Rising Campaigners Acquitted Over Müller Dairy Blockades Following Landmark Public Nuisance Ruling
content:
Six Animal Rising campaigners have today (22/09/26) been formally acquitted of all remaining charges relating to blockades of dairy giant Müller during the group’s 2022 ‘Stop the Supply’ campaign. The Crown Prosecution Service offered no evidence against them after an Animal Rising Supreme Court victory earlier this year which clarified how public nuisance law applies to campaigners on private land.

The six had faced charges of public nuisance and conspiracy to commit criminal damage relating to actions at Müller’s Droitwich site on 6 and 8 September 2022.
